To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stakeholder salience and institutional pressures are two key factors that influence the implementation of EHR systems for healthcare integration.
the salience and influence of key stakeholders are important factors in EHR implementation.
the salience of different stakeholder groups and the influence of different institutional logics can help explain the successful implementation of the NEHR initiative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the implementation process of EHR systems is influenced by stakeholders and institutional factors.
understanding the salience and influence of different stakeholder groups in EHR implementation.
understanding the role and influence of stakeholders and institutions in the implementation of EHRs for IT-enabled healthcare integration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the implementation of the NEHR in Singapore has been successful due to the involvement and support of the various stakeholders, and the strong institutional influences in Singapore.
stakeholder theory and institutional theory can be combined to explain the implementation of EHRs in a healthcare integration context.
the salience and the institutional influences of key stakeholders have played important roles in the implementation of NEHR in Singapore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salience of stakeholders and institutional influences are important factors to consider in the implementation of EHR systems.
EHR systems can be implemented for healthcare integration effectively when there is an alignment of the salience and legitimacy of different stakeholders.

stakeholder theory and institutional theory are both important in the context of EHR implementation, but the former is more relevant to the early stage of implementation while the latter is more important to the later stage of implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stakeholders should be involved in all phases of an EHR implementation project to facilitate the buy-in and to ensure a successful implementation.
the government should take the lead in EHR implementation and ensure the buy-in of other stakeholders, such as healthcare providers, patients, and the general public.

EHR implementation should not be considered as a one-time event but as a continuous process of change, and that the buy-in from different stakeholders should be considered throughout the entire process.
